sessions.phase_label: Landing-page and SaaS UI scope definition
Responsive handoff and broader website/UI foundation
Website implementation feedback, footer, and access-page design

requirements.title: Landing-Page Sign-Up Call to Action
requirements.definition: The landing page must expose a sign-up action that allows the business to establish an operational web presence.
requirements.boundary_note: The sign-up action is independently testable and can change without changing the page's visual theme, content sequence, or responsive layout.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Visual System
requirements.definition: The landing page must use a coherent visual treatment governing its dark theme, hero presentation, typography, colors, imagery, and primary CTA emphasis.
requirements.boundary_note: Theme, typography, color, and hero emphasis form one tightly coupled visual mechanism; content ordering, navigation, footer behavior, and responsive rules are independently changeable Requirements.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Content Structure
requirements.definition: The landing page must organize its marketing content as a single-page experience, including an early How It Works section that presents the agent setup sequence.
requirements.boundary_note: The individual How It Works steps are content within one ordered explanatory section rather than independently evolving product mechanisms.

requirements.title: Responsive Landing-Page Layout
requirements.definition: The landing page must provide usable desktop, tablet, mobile, and intermediate-width layouts without content overlap.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement owns landing-page viewport behavior and overlap prevention; reusable responsive guidance for other pages is a separate implementation-foundation Requirement.

requirements.title: Shared Visual Foundation for Website Pages
requirements.definition: Follow-on website pages must use a consistent visual foundation related to the landing page, including an agreed page theme and shared chrome treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement governs cross-page visual consistency; the behavior and content of the header navigation and footer remain independently modifiable Requirements.

requirements.title: Website Header Navigation
requirements.definition: The website must provide the currently approved header-navigation behavior for accessing landing-page sections or associated pages.
requirements.boundary_note: Header navigation changed independently from the footer and page theme, including removal from the short landing page and later addition of a menu for associated pages.

requirements.title: Shared Website Footer
requirements.definition: The website must provide a shared responsive footer containing the approved company details, navigation links, social links, copyright notice, and visual background treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: Footer content, responsive layout, and background treatment are attributes of one shared footer mechanism; the behavior of linked legal documents is independently testable.

requirements.title: Legal Document Access
requirements.definition: Standard legal and policy links must provide access to the corresponding documents, including opening the currently PDF-based pages in another browser tab.
requirements.boundary_note: Link presentation belongs to the header or footer, while document-opening behavior can fail or change independently and therefore owns a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Website Implementation Stack
requirements.definition: The live website must use plain HTML with Tailwind CSS rather than Astro.
requirements.boundary_note: The technology choice is independent from visual design assets, design tokens, and responsive acceptance behavior.

requirements.title: Web Design-System Specification
requirements.definition: Implementation must be supported by a concrete design-system specification covering color tokens, typography, spacing, radii, borders, font files, font identities and weights, and maximum content width.
requirements.boundary_note: The requested values form one reusable design-system artifact; whether they are physically incorporated into the existing brand-guide document remains unresolved.

requirements.title: Cross-Page Responsive Design Rules
requirements.definition: The website must use reusable responsive guidance and breakpoints for follow-on pages and layouts beyond the initial landing page.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement owns reusable cross-page rules; concrete desktop, tablet, and mobile behavior of the landing page remains under the landing-page responsive Requirement.

requirements.title: AWS Cognito Sign-In Page Styling
requirements.definition: The AWS Cognito-generated sign-in experience must be visually customized with Actia branding and an approved background while preserving Cognito-provided authentication behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: Authentication functionality is supplied by Cognito, while this Requirement concerns the independently evolving visual customization of that page.

requirements.title: Account Provisioning Wizard Styling
requirements.definition: The account-provisioning wizard must use the approved branded background and visual rules for typography, colors, active steps, controls, panel dimensions, and portrait and landscape layouts.
requirements.boundary_note: Wizard functionality is already being implemented separately; this Requirement owns its visual and responsive treatment rather than the underlying provisioning workflow.

requirements.title: Console Shell Visual Design
requirements.definition: The Console shell and main canvas must have a coherent branded layout and styling for the header, shell navigation, footer, fonts, colors, icons, surfaces, and light and dark modes.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement is limited to the shared shell and canvas treatment; application screens, navigation-panel organization, and button styling can evolve independently.

requirements.title: Console Navigation Panel Structure
requirements.definition: The Console must organize shell-level and application-level navigation without competing side panels, with the final nesting and placement approach to be resolved.
requirements.boundary_note: Panel placement and nesting can be modified or tested independently from the Console's overall theme and from individual button appearance.

requirements.title: Console Button Visual Style
requirements.definition: Console buttons must receive an approved treatment for color, shape, size, corner radius, and optional icon use.
requirements.boundary_note: Button appearance has its own design alternatives and acceptance criteria and can change without redesigning the broader Console shell.

requirements.title: Platform Solution Description Page
requirements.definition: The website must include an associated page presenting a solution description for the Actia platform.
requirements.boundary_note: The platform and agent solution descriptions occupy separate pages and can be revised independently; production of the page's diagram is also a distinct asset obligation.

requirements.title: Agent Solution Description Page
requirements.definition: The website must include an associated page presenting a solution description for Actia agents.
requirements.boundary_note: The agent solution page has content and assets distinct from the platform solution page and may be modified independently.

requirements.title: Customer and Staff Communication Diagram
requirements.definition: The first solution-page diagram must be converted into a production-ready website asset and use the approved customer and staff communication labels.
requirements.boundary_note: This diagram has its own content labels and production work, separate from the second diagram's directional cycle.

requirements.title: Clockwise Cycle Diagram
requirements.definition: The second solution-page diagram must be converted into a production-ready website asset with directional arrows running clockwise around its cycle.
requirements.boundary_note: Arrow direction and cyclical presentation are independent acceptance criteria not shared by the customer and staff communication diagram.

unresolved_candidates.description: The freelancer proposed retaining or removing a contact form and asked whether pricing information should be added, but no supplied client message clearly resolves either proposal.
The design-system values are clearly needed, but it is unresolved whether revising the existing brand-guide document is itself an accepted deliverable or only a suggested packaging option.

The client requested rough code for additional pages, but later context says Cognito generates the Sign In page and the Provisioning Wizard already functions; the exact remaining coding obligation versus visual-asset obligation is not safely separable from the supplied evidence.
